_readme: THE DEMO'S BIRTH DATA — the stores and the coffee catalogue, as DATA. `bin/seed.mjs` reads this file and
drives the port; nothing here is code, and no rule about products lives in the script.
⚠️ THIS IS NOT A SEED, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS DELIBERATE: no full seed, because it is CLEARER how to fill
the demo in once the whole thing stands up. What is here is the MINIMUM that
makes the demo stand: the stores, and the six coffees the coffee store lists on its home. There is no
importer, no generated mass, no customers, no orders. The real seed is a later slice, and it will be
written from what the finished demo turns out to need rather than from a guess made now.
⚠️ WHAT THE SOURCE DOCUMENT PROMISES AND DOES NOT CARRY. `DEMO2-CATALOGO-CAFE.md` opens with '6 cafés
listados DIRETO na home + 3 coadjuvantes para o compre-junto' and then tables only the six. The three
supporting products are named nowhere in it, and the photo folder holds six images. They are NOT invented
here: `recommendations` is on this box's composition list and its bought-together pairing has nothing to
pair with until somebody writes those three down.
MONEY IS IN CENTS, always, and never a float. `amount: 4290` is R$ 42,90.
THE SKU AXES are the product's own options, and 'Moagem' is the one the demo exists to show: it is
labelled by the customer's METHOD ('Grãos' · 'Filtrado' · 'Espresso'), not by particle size, because the
shopper knows how they brew and does not know what 'fina' means.
★ FOUR PHOTOGRAPHS PER COFFEE, AND THE CONVENTION IS POSITION. `PdpCoffee.tsx:5` states it: `photos[0]` is
the bag (the transparent shot the buy box draws) and `photos[1..3]` are the story — one wide 4:3 frame and
two squares. `photo` (singular) is still here and still names the bag: it is what `photos[0]` must be, and
the seed falls back to it for a product that declares no list, so nothing regressed when the list arrived.
⚠️ THE THREE STORY FRAMES DO NOT EXIST ON DISK YET — `seed/photos/` holds one picture per coffee. They are
declared anyway, under the FINAL name the merchant will produce, and the seed serves a generated stand-in
from `seed/placeholder-media/` until the real file lands: shipping something WRONG beats shipping nothing,
because a hole nobody can see is a hole nobody knows to fill. Drop the real file into `seed/photos/`
under the name written here and nothing else changes — the next run re-points the picture.
★ THE NINE CUSTOM FIELDS are the ones the shop's "Características" panel draws, and they are all declared on
all six, with a real value.
⚠️⚠️ A MARKER FOR "THIS DATA IS MISSING" MUST NEVER TRAVEL INSIDE THE VALUE, and this file learned it the
expensive way. A50 says a hole must be RECOGNISABLE — and the reader it exists for is the OPERATOR, who is
going to close it. The slice before this one wrote the marker into the value (`Produtor: Vários produtores
(placeholder)`, `SCA 82 (placeholder)`), and a product custom field is served by the anonymous read face and
printed on the shop window: the shopper read the word "placeholder" in about six places per page, in the
one screen that exists to make them trust the coffee. The marker had reached the only reader it was never
meant for.
A marker belongs where only the operator looks: the seed's own report, a field of its own, or a picture the
merchant must replace (`seed/placeholder-media/` — that one is deliberate and stays). It never
belongs in a value the port publishes. So the rule for THIS file is the plain one: write the content, or
omit the field. This is a demonstration shop — a fictional producer and a fictional farm ARE the content,
and they are what a demo is for. `seed/coffee.test.mjs` fails on the word, in any of the nine or in a story.

stores.name: Forge Outlet
stores.why: Created by `provision-ref` at bootstrap, not by this script — a first store is bootstrap, a second is data. It is listed here so the file is the whole picture, and the script CHECKS it rather than creating it.

stores.name: Forge
stores.why: Tenant 1's second store, on the vanilla theme. It is the control: the Outlet's whole thesis is that a theme plus data plus composition is enough, and a thesis with nothing to be compared against is a claim.

stores.name: Forge Café · Balcão
stores.why: The counter the totem serves — the coffee shop's SECOND store, on the same tenant as `cafe`. It is created by `seed/totem.mjs`, not by the store step, and it is listed here so this file is the whole picture of the topology (which is what the `outlet` entry above already claims to be, and was not while this one was missing). No theme: the totem is an app of its own and resolves none.

stores.name: Forge Café
stores.why: The coffee store, and it lives on the SECOND tenant — `forgecafe` — with the counter beside it. ⚠️ THIS FIELD USED TO SAY THE OPPOSITE, and the sentence it carried is why this demo was one tenant for weeks: it claimed a second tenant would need a second admin container, because the admin is pinned by FORGE_ADMIN_TENANT. That was FALSE. `read.admin.by_host` (M4-ADMIN-HOST) resolves the tenant from the hostname — with the PORT significant — and `platform.admin_host.set` writes that map, so ONE admin deployment serves N tenants; `compose.yml` says so on the FORGE_ADMIN_TENANT line itself ('leave it EMPTY for a box that serves several brands by hostname'). It also pointed at a README section that does not exist. A shoe brand and a coffee shop are not one company, and the topology now says so.
stores._vocabulary_why: E1 — the store's OWN words, as DATA and never as theme. Two keys of different species on purpose: `cart` is a NOUN the kit interpolates only after a bare verb, and `cart_empty_title` is a whole SENTENCE because Portuguese makes the noun's gender load-bearing — a shop that says 'Sacola' needs 'Sua sacola está vazia', not 'Seu sacola está vazio'. A string list that tried to do that agreement would be doing grammar.

products.title: Forge Alvorada
products.subtitle: O blend da casa
products.description: O café de todo dia. Torra média, corpo redondo e doçura fácil — chocolate ao leite, caramelo e nozes. Vem da Mogiana Paulista, onde a altitude e a colheita tardia dão ao grão o açúcar que sustenta a xícara sem precisar de nada.

custom_fields.fazenda: Sítio Boa Esperança, Sítio Córrego Fundo e Fazenda Santa Luzia

content_sections.title: Quem plantou
content_sections.body: O Alvorada é um blend, e um blend tem mais de um dono: ele nasce de produtores da Mogiana Paulista que entregam à mesma cooperativa e colhem tarde, quando o grão já carrega o açúcar que sustenta a xícara. São três famílias: os Prado, no Sítio Boa Esperança, entregam desde a safra de 1998; os Tanaka, no Córrego Fundo, secam em terreiro de cimento e viram o café de duas em duas horas; e os Vasconcelos, na Santa Luzia, são os últimos a colher todo ano — é deles a doçura que fecha o blend.

products.title: Forge Serra do Caparaó
products.subtitle: Microlote single origin
products.description: Um microlote da Serra do Caparaó, no Espírito Santo, a 1.200 metros. Catuaí amarelo, lavado, torra clara: mel, maçã verde e um floral que aparece quando a xícara esfria um pouco. 86 pontos SCA.

content_sections.title: Quem plantou
content_sections.body: O microlote vem da Serra do Caparaó, no Espírito Santo, a 1.200 metros, onde o Catuaí amarelo amadurece devagar e é lavado no mesmo dia da colheita. Quem colhe são Sebastião e Marlene Ferraz, no Sítio Alto do Caparaó: dezoito hectares na encosta, colheita seletiva a dedo e um lavador que o Sebastião montou com a bomba de um trator velho.

products.title: Forge Cerrado Mineiro
products.subtitle: Denominação de origem
products.description: Do Cerrado Mineiro, a primeira denominação de origem do café brasileiro. Natural, torra média: chocolate 70%, avelã e um fundo de cana que fica na boca. O café que combina com qualquer coisa que você já tenha na despensa.

content_sections.title: Quem plantou
content_sections.body: O Cerrado Mineiro foi a primeira denominação de origem do café brasileiro: a região responde por ele com um selo, e o lote chega pela cooperativa que reúne os sítios do alto. O desta safra é da Fazenda Vereda Grande, em Patrocínio, que entrega à cooperativa desde 1994 e seca o café em terreiro suspenso antes de mandá-lo para o armazém.

products.title: Forge Noturno
products.subtitle: Blend intenso
products.description: Torra escura, feita para o leite e para o espresso curto. Cacau, melaço e especiarias; corpo alto e amargor limpo. É o café que não some debaixo de meio litro de leite.

custom_fields.fazenda: Sítio Pedra Branca (Carmo de Minas) e Sítio das Palmeiras (Franca)

content_sections.title: Quem plantou
content_sections.body: O Noturno é feito para o leite, e por isso é montado: grãos do Sul de Minas e da Mogiana entram na mesma torra escura até o corpo aguentar meio litro de leite sem sumir. O corpo vem do Sítio Pedra Branca, dos Rezende, em Carmo de Minas; o melaço vem do Sítio das Palmeiras, dos Okamoto, em Franca. Separados nenhum dos dois aguentaria o leite — juntos, aguentam.

skus.why: The de/por promotion the catalogue asks for. `compare_at_amount` is the SKU's own field, so the discount is a fact about the price and not a rule an app has to be installed to see.

products.title: Forge Descafeinado
products.subtitle: Swiss Water
products.description: Descafeinado pelo processo Swiss Water — água, tempo e paciência, sem solvente. Torra média, biscoito e chocolate. O café das nove da noite que continua sendo café.

content_sections.title: Quem plantou
content_sections.body: O grão é do Sul de Minas e viaja antes de torrar: o processo Swiss Water tira a cafeína com água e tempo, sem solvente, e devolve um café que continua sendo café. O grão é da Fazenda Santa Rita, dos Nogueira, em Três Pontas — a mesma família que planta o Catuaí amarelo há três gerações e que passou a separar um lote só para descafeinar quando a filha mais velha parou de tomar café à noite.

products.title: Forge Edição do Produtor
products.subtitle: Sítio Boa Vista · Dona Cida · Mantiqueira de Minas
products.description: Dona Cida colhe no Sítio Boa Vista, na Mantiqueira de Minas, e seca o café em terreiro suspenso por catorze dias. Bourbon amarelo, honey, 88 pontos SCA: jasmim, pêssego e rapadura. Lote numerado, e quando acaba, acabou.

content_sections.title: Quem plantou
content_sections.body: Dona Cida colhe no Sítio Boa Vista, na Mantiqueira de Minas, e seca o café em terreiro suspenso por catorze dias — cada lote sai numerado e assinado por ela. Quando acaba, acabou: a edição seguinte é outra colheita e outro número.

skus.why: The scarcity the catalogue asks for — 'restam 14'. It is real stock and not a label: the shelf that says 'Acabando!' reads the same number the checkout refuses to oversell.

_custom_fields_why: ★★ THE COFFEE SHOP'S VOCABULARY, AND IT LIVES BESIDE THE COFFEES BECAUSE A CUSTOM FIELD IS PER TENANT.
⛔ WHERE IT USED TO LIVE AND WHAT THAT COST, measured on the bench of 02/09. This list was a `FIELDS`
const inside `bin/seed.mjs`, declared by a `customFields()` that ran for EVERY tenant the script was
pointed at — and box-up points it at both. So the footwear tenant's product form offered TORRA, FAZENDA,
PRODUTOR, PONTUAÇÃO SCA, NOTAS SENSORIAIS, VARIEDADE, PROCESSO, REGIÃO and ALTITUDE: every shoe in the
shop offered a roast. Proven by the registry itself, not inferred — all nine sit in
`forgeco.custom_field_definition` with `source = 'merchant'`, which is this script's signature.
★ THE MIRROR IS THE SAME SHAPE WITH A DIFFERENT OWNER, and knowing which is which is the point: the
eleven footwear fields (AMORTECIMENTO, CANO, DROP MM, …) carry `source = 'app:demo-data'` — the DATASET's
`custom-fields.json`, materialised by `extension.install`. They reached the coffee tenant because step 9
of box-up installed that app there, not because anything declared them here. That half is fixed by
`dataset` in seed/box.json; this half is fixed by moving these nine next to the products that use them.
⚠️ IT IS DECLARED BEFORE ANY PRODUCT WRITES ONE. `catalog.product.create` accepts an UNDECLARED metadata
key happily and then hides it from every faceting and PDP feature that reads declarations — silent, and
exactly the kind of thing found three slices later. `seed/outlet.mjs` carries the opposite lesson at
length: the footwear vocabulary is the DATASET's and this repository stopped declaring it. Same rule,
_products_store_why: WHICH STORE SELLS THEM. `catalog.product.create` makes a product of the TENANT; being on sale in a store is a second, separate act (`catalog.product.publish`) — and D1 did the first and not the second, so the six coffees existed and no shop showed them. Measured: `read.products?store=<cafe>` answered 0 with all six created. A product is not a listing.
_stock_why: STOCK, and D1 left it at zero. `catalog.sku.create` prices a SKU; it does not stock it, and a shop whose every SKU is at 0 refuses `cart.add_line` with `insufficient_stock · available: 0` — measured. So each SKU is stocked at this number unless it declares its own `on_hand` (the Edição do Produtor declares 14, because its scarcity is part of the demo). 40 is a demo's number: enough that nobody hits a wall, small enough that the 'Acabando!' shelf still means something.
_stock_pool_why: ⛔⛔ THE STOCK POOL — PRODUCTS OF THIS TENANT THAT NO STORE SELLS, AND THAT IS THE POINT. Do not
'fix' them by publishing them: publishing one is what breaks the thing they exist for.
WHO ASKS FOR THEM. The 180-day past of this box is written by the `demo-data` app inside the kernel, and
its plan drives products into the three states the admin's stock screen shows — `out` (every stocked SKU
at zero), `partial` (SOME at zero, not all) and `low` (1..5). It takes them from a POOL it defines as the
products NONE of the selling SKUs belong to (`apps/api/src/seed-history.ts:477`), because the generator
ZEROES their stock: doing that to something a shop sells would put an out-of-stock item on the shelf and
make the same run order goods it had just taken away. The three states need 3 + 4 + 6 = 13 products
(`extensions/demo-data/history/plan.ts:489-491`), and at least 4 of them must be MULTI-SKU, because
`partial` is only expressible on a product with siblings. Fewer than 13 is a REFUSAL, by name:
history plan: the stock pool has 11 product(s) and the three alert states need 13. Widen it (it must
also stay disjoint from what the stores sell).
⚠️ AND THAT IS WHAT BLOCKED THIS BRAND'S PAST ENTIRELY — no past, no dashboard, no order queue, no
revenue series, on the tenant the demo opens on.
★★ WHY THIS KEY EXISTS AT ALL, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN THE TWO PRODUCTS IN IT. Measured on the bench of
2026-09-03: this tenant holds 21 products and EVERY ONE of them is published by the counter, so on paper
the pool is empty. It was not — it held 11 — and the reason is an ACCIDENT OF SAMPLING: the history
reads only the first 40 sellable SKUs per store, ordered by id (`CATALOG_PER_STORE`,
`apps/api/src/seed-history.ts:141`), and the counter has 63. The 11 were simply the overflow, the
products whose SKUs sort past the 40th. A pool that is the leftover of a LIMIT disappears the day the
catalogue shrinks, the day a price changes an id, the day somebody re-orders this file — and the past
would start failing again with nothing anywhere saying why. So the pool is DECLARED here, with its
reason beside it, and `seed/pool.test.mjs` measures it with the kernel's own rule.
⚠️ WHAT IS STILL AN ACCIDENT, AND IS REPORTED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: two declared products bring the pool
to exactly 13, so the generator uses ALL of it — the 11 overflow products included. Eleven items the
counter really does sell will therefore come out of the seed at low/partial/zero stock (`caneca-
esmaltada` is the one that goes fully to zero). Making the pool truly disjoint from both assortments
needs 13 products no store sells, i.e. eleven more than are here. That is a call this repository has not
made — it is eleven more photographs — and until it is, this is a demo whose counter shows some sold-out lines.
THE SHOP'S OWN STORY FOR THEM: two classics the bar knows how to make and is not offering this season.
A catalogue is larger than a menu, which is exactly the fact the stock screen exists to manage.
⚠️ ONE PHOTOGRAPH EACH, AND NO STAND-IN. These two arrived from the merchant with their real picture
(2026-09-03), so unlike the six coffees they declare no `photos` list and no story frames: a product no
shopper can reach has no page to tell a story on. `seed/placeholder-media/` is therefore not consulted
for them, and `bin/make-placeholders.mjs` does not grow three frames per pool product.
⚠️ SINGLE SKU EACH, ON PURPOSE. `partial` needs 4 multi-SKU products and the pool already carries 10, so
there is slack; inventing a size axis for a drink that is not on any menu would be data pretending to be
a decision.

products.title: Americano
products.description: Espresso alongado com água quente. Mesma dose, xícara maior, corpo mais leve — o café de quem fica.

products.title: Macchiato
products.description: Espresso marcado com uma colher de espuma. Entre o curto e o cappuccino, e mais perto do curto.
